clauses.mechanism: spent_on_issue: amendment of the list attached to Executive Order No. 12950, complete on signing by the President
clauses.reason: The only operative sentence says the list of Labor Organizations attached to Executive Order No. 12950 is amended to include the International Brotherhood of Firemen & Oilers. That amendment was complete when the President signed the order on February 24, 1995 (held original, 60 FR 11011), and the order has no continuing command, so the command ended on signing; the inserted entry survives only as part of Executive Order 12950's list.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12952 (February 24, 1995; 60 FR 11011) has one operative sentence: it amends Executive Order No. 12950 so that "the list of Labor Organizations" attached to that order includes "International Brotherhood of Firemen & Oilers". Executive Order 12950 (February 22, 1995) established an emergency board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act. The amendment is a self-executing act that was complete when the President signed on February 24, 1995; the order contains no continuing command, standing rule or duty. The entry it inserted lives on only inside Executive Order 12950's list, so its further life belongs to that order and is recorded under savings. Searches of held texts for the number 12952 found only the order's own Federal Register text, the Federal Register daily-contents entry (fr-95-5129) and an APP transcription; no later instrument names it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The held original is a single operative sentence with no condition or duration, and the order has no revival, delay or conditional effective date. The three bounded searches and the held-text search for the number 12952 located no earlier or later instrument that revokes, supersedes or amends it, so no earlier end competes with the date of signing.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the list amendment: no report, delegation, funding or continuing duty.","savings_check":"The surviving effect is the inserted union name inside Executive Order 12950's list; it is carried by the parent and is stated under savings as transferred.","scope_check":"The order has one scope (the whole order is the one amendment of the list). No part of it was separately revoked or amended."}

savings.reason: The inserted name became part of the list of labor organizations attached to Executive Order 12950 and is carried inside that order, not in Executive Order 12952. By its held Federal Register text Executive Order 12950 established an emergency board that was to report within 30 days of its creation on February 22, 1995 and to terminate on submission of that report, with the section 9A(c) status-quo period running 120 days from creation. No dossier evidence id holds the parent's end or the report date, so the parent's end is not asserted; the amendment's own command was spent on issue.
